elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 now reads "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory." The prohibition ("shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire") and its term-plus-twenty-four-month tail are gone, and § 12.3 is retained ("Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete ... commitment"). No field-of-use or territory restriction on Customer remains; the deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" is ok. The separate no-hire covenant at the other § 12.4 is a non-solicitation matter outside this checklist.','

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: vacuously satisfied because no restriction on Customer survives. The rendered § 12.4 is a permission, not a covenant, so there is no product scope to name.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: vacuously satisfied. The "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" temporal anchor was struck along with the prohibition; no covenant remains to which a term limit could attach.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: vacuously satisfied. The 24-month post-term tail (walk-away territory) is deleted and no duration mechanic remains.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: vacuously satisfied — and affirmatively addressed. § 12.4 as rendered expressly permits Customer to "develop" competing products, reinforced by § 12.3.

Conditional element: vacuously satisfied — § 12.4 as rendered expressly permits Customer to "acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor," and § 12.3 preserves Customer's freedom to acquire.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the comment. The offer of a narrowed term-only, 12-month, carve-out fallback sits in the margin comment where it belongs and does not weaken the rendered text.

Fallback elements are recorded as met on a vacuous basis only — there is no surviving restriction whose scope, duration or carve-outs could be tested. This does not indicate that a fallback restriction was drafted.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only the offending sentence in the duplicate-numbered § 12.4, keeps the section number and the residual scope wording, adds no survival tail, expense, procedure or remedy language, and removes no Customer-favourable text (§ 12.3, including the no-hire and MFN acknowledgements, is retained verbatim).

Drafting note (not a minimality failure): the converted § 12.4 permission substantively restates § 12.3's broader "Nothing restricts Customer" language, so the two now overlap. Striking § 12.4 in its entirety would achieve the same preferred result without redundant operative language; if the counterparty resists an affirmative permission, deletion is the cleaner fallback drafting route.

Intent preserved: the edit removes the direct contradiction between the old § 12.4 and § 12.3 rather than creating one, leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and does not disturb the separate no-hire covenant in the other § 12.4, exclusivity, pricing, term or remedy mechanics.

Severity retained at high: the original clause was walk-away (undefined "any product or service that competes with Vendor," 24-month post-term tail, no carve-outs), so the deviation classification is correct.
